name: agent-bom-lookup
description: Read-only package and advisory lookups from agent-bom on a public server with no sign-in: check one package version for known vulnerabilities and malicious-package advisories, or look up one CVE, GHSA or OSV advisory. Sends only the package name, ecosystem and version, or the advisory id.

interface.longDescription:
Look up known vulnerabilities and malicious-package advisories without leaving the chat. Ask whether a package version is safe to install, or what a CVE or GHSA advisory is and which version fixes it.

Two read-only tools:
- check: one package name and version in an application ecosystem such as npm, PyPI, Go, Maven or crates.io, checked against OSV.dev, GitHub security advisories and agent-bom's advisory data, including known-malicious packages.
- intel_lookup: one CVE, GHSA or OSV id from the server's advisory database (OSV for PyPI and npm, CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS), loaded when the server starts. A miss reports what the database covers instead of claiming the advisory does not exist.

What is sent: only the package name, ecosystem and version, or the advisory id, that the assistant passes to a tool. The server sends package coordinates to OSV.dev, to the GitHub public security-advisory API and, for npm and PyPI, to that public registry to resolve a latest version and confirm the version exists. It never asks for files, code, credentials or chat history, and there is no account or sign-in.

Limits: lookups only. It does not scan your computer, repositories, MCP configuration or cloud accounts; the open-source agent-bom CLI does that on your own machine. OS packages (deb, apk, rpm) are not supported here. Rate limits are shared by all anonymous users.
defaultPrompt: Is event-stream 3.3.6 from npm safe to install?
Does requests 2.19.0 on PyPI have known vulnerabilities?
What is CVE-2024-3651 and which version fixes it?

positive.description: Flags a known-malicious npm release before install
positive.prompt: Is event-stream 3.3.6 from npm safe to install?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check for event-stream version 3.3.6 in the npm ecosystem. Says not to install it because it is a known-malicious release, cites advisory GHSA-mh6f-8j2x-4483, and suggests removing or replacing it.

positive.description: Lists known vulnerabilities for an old PyPI version with fixed versions
positive.prompt: Does requests 2.19.0 on PyPI have known vulnerabilities?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check with package requests@2.19.0 and ecosystem pypi. Reports that it is vulnerable, names CVE-2018-18074 (high, fixed in 2.20.0) among the advisories, and recommends upgrading to the newest fixed version the tool reports.

positive.description: Accepts the version as a separate argument for an npm package
positive.prompt: Check the npm package lodash version 4.17.20 for vulnerabilities.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check with package lodash, version 4.17.20 and ecosystem npm. Reports that it is vulnerable, including CVE-2021-23337 (high, fixed in 4.17.21), and gives the fixed versions the tool returns.

positive.description: Explains a CVE and its fix from the advisory database
positive.prompt: What is CVE-2024-3651 and which version fixes it?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls intel_lookup with advisory_id CVE-2024-3651. Explains it is a medium-severity denial-of-service issue in the Python idna package, recorded as GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h, fixed in idna 3.7.

positive.description: Looks up a GHSA id and lists the affected packages
positive.prompt: Look up advisory GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm. Which packages does it affect?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls intel_lookup with advisory_id GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm. Reports a high-severity command injection in lodash (CVE-2021-23337) and lists the affected packages the tool returns, including lodash and lodash-es, with their fixed versions.

negative.description: Unrelated request; no tool should be called
negative.prompt: What will the weather be like in Paris this weekend?

negative.description: Asks for a local scan, which this plugin cannot do; it should not call a tool or claim to have scanned anything
negative.prompt: Scan all the MCP servers configured on my computer for security problems.

negative.description: General coding help that is not a package or advisory lookup
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that sorts a list of dictionaries by one key.

publication.release_notes: First release: two read-only lookups, check and intel_lookup, on a public server with no sign-in.
